land.text: the fortress on the Rock of Monaco, held by the Grimaldi 'under the sovereignty of the Republic of Genoa'

predecessors.note: Monaco page infobox: 'House of Grimaldi, under the sovereignty of the Republic of Genoa: 8 January 1297'. The Rock had been a Genoese colony since 1215. Cliopatria's first Monaco shape is 1642; the dossier starts at the Grimaldi seizure of 1297 and adds new keyframes for 1297-1641. The Grimaldi lost the Rock to Genoa four times before 1419 (List of rulers of Monaco: Genoese control 10 April 1301 to 12 September 1331, 15 August 1357 to January 1395, 19 December 1395 to 11 May 1397, 5 November 1402 to 5 June 1419), so Genoa is the counterpart of eight gain and loss events.

capitals.name: Monaco (Monaco-Ville, the Rock)
capitals.note: The Rock, held by Francesco Grimaldi from 8 January 1297 until the Genoese retook it on 10 April 1301 (List of rulers of Monaco). The Monaco page's infobox gives 'Monaco (city-state)' as capital; the coordinates are the gazetteer's Monaco place (7.41, 43.74). No capital is given for 1301-1330: the Rock was 'Under Genoese control from 10 April 1301 to 12 September 1331' and no page opened names another Grimaldi seat.

capitals.name: Monaco (Monaco-Ville, the Rock)
capitals.note: The Rock retaken by Charles I on 12 September 1331 (List of rulers of Monaco).

capitals.name: Monaco (Monaco-Ville, the Rock)
capitals.note: The Rock in Grimaldi hands from January to 19 December 1395 (List of rulers of Monaco). No capital is given for 1357-1394 and 1396: the Rock was Genoese, the Grimaldi kept Menton and Roquebrune, and no page opened names their seat.

capitals.name: Monaco (Monaco-Ville, the Rock)
capitals.note: The Rock regained on 11 May 1397 (List of rulers of Monaco). No capital is given for 1402-1418: the Rock was 'Under Genoese control from 5 November 1402 to 5 June 1419' and no page opened names the Grimaldi seat in those years.

capitals.name: Monaco (Monaco-Ville, the Rock)
capitals.note: The prince's seat stayed on the Rock from the repurchase of 5 June 1419; during the French annexation 1793-1814 the principality was administered from France (Alpes-Maritimes) and no separate seat is recorded.

rulers.name: Francesco (François) Grimaldi
rulers.title: Lord of Monaco
rulers.note: 8 January 1297 to 10 April 1301; his cousin Rainier I (Lord of Cagnes) is listed without reign dates.

rulers.name: Charles I
rulers.title: Lord of Monaco
rulers.note: 12 September 1331 to 15 August 1357; co-ruled with Anthony I from 29 June 1352. The Rock was Genoese 1301-1331; the list gives no reign dates for Rainier II and Gabriel, co-rulers whose Genoese-held lordship lasted from 15 August 1357 to January 1395.

rulers.name: Louis (first reign)
rulers.title: Lord of Monaco
rulers.note: January to 19 December 1395, ruling jointly with Jean I.

rulers.name: Jean I
rulers.title: Lord of Monaco
rulers.note: 5 June 1419 to 8 May 1454; ruled jointly with his brothers Ambroise and Antoine until 1427, then bought them out; 'On 20 November 1441, Jean gained sovereignty for Monaco'.

rulers.name: Claudine
rulers.title: Lord of Monaco
rulers.note: July 1457 to 16 March 1458; abdicated in favour of her cousin Lamberto.

rulers.name: Jean II
rulers.title: Lord of Monaco
rulers.note: March 1494 to 11 October 1505; murdered by his brother Lucien.

rulers.name: Lucien
rulers.title: Lord of Monaco
rulers.note: 11 October 1505 to 22 August 1523; murdered his brother Jean II.

rulers.name: Honoré I
rulers.title: Lord of Monaco
rulers.note: 22 August 1523 to 7 October 1581; regency under Augustine Grimaldi, bishop of Grasse, to 14 April 1532.

rulers.name: Honoré II
rulers.title: Lord, from 1612 Prince of Monaco
rulers.note: 29 November 1604 to 10 January 1662; regency under Francis Landi of Valdetare until 1616; Monaco recognised as a sovereign principality by Philip IV of Spain in 1633.

rulers.name: Jacques I
rulers.title: Prince of Monaco
rulers.note: 29 December 1731 to 7 November 1733 (abdicated); left the country in May 1732.

rulers.name: Honoré III
rulers.title: Prince of Monaco
rulers.note: 7 November 1733 to 19 January 1793 as the list page ends his reign; his uncle Antoine Grimaldi was regent until 28 November 1784. Monaco was annexed by France in 1793 and the list names French commissioners, not a prince, for 1793-1814.

rulers.name: Honoré IV
rulers.title: Prince of Monaco
rulers.note: 30 May 1814 to 16 February 1819 (list page); the principality was restored in May 1814.

rulers.name: Charles III
rulers.title: Prince of Monaco
rulers.note: 20 June 1856 to 10 September 1889; Menton and Roquebrune were ceded in 1861.

correction.text: the fortress on the Rock of Monaco: 'Francesco Grimaldi seized the Rock' (History of Monaco); 'Monaco was first ruled by a member of the House of Grimaldi in 1297'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria has no Monaco shape before 1642. The lordship is the Rock and its immediate land; the whole modern country is used as the nearest nameable region (a reading, the page gives no boundary). Francesco Grimaldi holds the Rock from 8 January 1297 under the sovereignty of the Republic of Genoa (infobox) until the Genoese retake it on 10 April 1301 (List of rulers of Monaco: 'Under Genoese control from 10 April 1301 to 12 September 1331'; Monaco page: 'Francesco was evicted a few years later by the Genoese forces'). Convention for this and the next keyframes: a keyframe starts in the year of the ledger event that creates it, so the month fields give the timing within the year.

correction.text: the Rock of Monaco, retaken from the Genoese: Charles I 'retook the Rock from the Genoese' (List of rulers of Monaco)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: nothing is drawn for 1301-1330 because the Rock was 'Under Genoese control from 10 April 1301 to 12 September 1331' and the Grimaldi held no other land that any page opened names (Menton comes in 1346). Charles I retakes the Rock on 12 September 1331 (List of rulers of Monaco; Charles I page: 'Charles retook the Rock on 12 September 1331').

correction.text: Monaco, Menton and Roquebrune: 'In 1355, Roccabruna fell under the control of the Grimaldi family of Monaco for five centuries' (Roquebrune page)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Roquebrune joins in 1355 (Roquebrune page; Charles I page: 'in 1355, he conquered the Lordship of Roquebrune'). The Rock, Menton and Roquebrune are all held for two years, until the death of Charles I on 15 August 1357.

correction.text: Menton and Roquebrune only: the Rock is 'Under Genoese control from 15 August 1357 to January 1395'; Rainier II 'Yielded Monaco to the besieging Genoese for 20,000 fl. but retained Menton and Roquebrune' (List of rulers of Monaco)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the Genoese retake the Rock after the death of Charles I on 15 August 1357 (Charles I page: the Rock 'was again conquered by the Genoese army'). The Grimaldi keep Menton and Roquebrune. The list page does not date the yielding for 20,000 fl.; the span rests on its 'Genoese control' line. The shape is two radii around the towns (a reading); at the grid's resolution they add little beyond the Monaco cell. No page names the Grimaldi seat in these years.

correction.text: Monaco, Menton and Roquebrune: Louis 'January 1395 - 19 December 1395' (List of rulers of Monaco)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the Grimaldi hold the Rock again from January 1395 (the Monaco page: 'in the late 1300s Genoa lost Monaco after fighting the Crown of Aragon over Corsica') and lose it on 19 December 1395.

correction.text: Menton and Roquebrune only: the Rock is 'Under Genoese control from 19 December 1395 to 11 May 1397' (List of rulers of Monaco)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the whole of 1396 is Genoese on the Rock; Menton and Roquebrune are read as kept by the Grimaldi on the strength of Rainier II's 'retained Menton and Roquebrune' (undated on the page).

correction.text: Monaco, Menton and Roquebrune: Louis '11 May 1397 - 5 November 1402' (List of rulers of Monaco)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the Rock regained on 11 May 1397 and held to 5 November 1402 (the year of that loss, 1402, belongs to the next keyframe).

correction.text: Menton and Roquebrune only: the Rock is 'Under Genoese control from 5 November 1402 to 5 June 1419' (List of rulers of Monaco)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the Genoese hold the Rock again from 5 November 1402 until the sons of Rainier II 'bought back Monaco from Genoa' on 5 June 1419. No page names the Grimaldi seat in these years.

correction.text: Monaco, Menton and Roquebrune: Jean, Ambroise and Antoine 'bought back Monaco from Genoa' (List of rulers of Monaco); 'In 1419, the Grimaldi family purchased Monaco from the Crown of Aragon' (Monaco page)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the three-place principality from the repurchase of 5 June 1419 to the Treaty of Péronne. The seller is disputed between the pages (Genoa on the list page, the Crown of Aragon on the Monaco page; see the ledger event and the notes). Jean I bought out his brothers in 1427 for the rule over Menton and Roquebrune, Milan occupied Monaco from 3 October to November 1436 (ledger), and 'On 20 November 1441, Jean gained sovereignty for Monaco' (list page). Spanish authority over Monaco from 1524 (History of Monaco: 'an autonomous state for about a century', with a Spanish garrison at the fortress) and Honoré II's recognition by Spain in 1633 (Monaco page) change the protector, not the extent.

correction.text: France recognised the prince's sovereignty over Monaco, Menton and Roquebrune (Article 6 of the Treaty of Péronne, 14 September 1641)

keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria area 141.0 km2 against roughly 40 km2 implied by the pages (Monaco infobox 2.084 km2 today; History of Monaco: the 1861 cession of Menton and Roquebrune was 'about 95% of its territory', so about 2.084/0.05 = 42 km2 before it): ratio far beyond two. The polygon is a cell-sized blob, not a survey; the land it names is right, the extent is not. This 1642-1644 shape is 23 km2 smaller than Cliopatria's 1645 shape (164.4 km2) and its east edge (7.47E) is west of the 1645 edge (7.55E), but the Treaty of Péronne already names all three places in 1641 and no page gives an acquisition in 1645, so the corrected extent is the same from 1419 to 1793 (the three places; the Rock itself was Genoese in 1357-1394, 1396 and 1402-1418, see the keyframes before 1419). The French fiefs given to Honoré II in compensation (Valentinois, Baux, Carladès and others) lie outside the principality and are not in the shape.

The polygon is a cell-sized blob, not a survey; the land it names is right, the extent is not. Same three places as the corrected 1642 shape; no page opened dates a change in 1645. The 1794-1813 gap in Cliopatria is right: Monaco was taken over by France in 1793 and restored in 1814.

The polygon is a cell-sized blob, not a survey; the land it names is right, the extent is not. History of Monaco: French control ran 'from 1793 to May 17, 1814'; the Monaco page's infobox adds 17 June 1814 'from occupation of the Sixth Coalition'. The polygon is a cell-sized blob, not a survey; the land it names is right, the extent is not. The row's name is wrong: Monaco was a principality throughout (Monaco page: 'Principality of Monaco'; no page calls it a kingdom); the 'Kingdom' is Cliopatria's label, and the row shares Wikidata Q235 with the Principality row, so the two rows are one state. History of Monaco adds the Treaty of Stupinigi (1817) confirming the Sardinian protectorate.

Use the named country. 1848-1860: Menton and Roquebrune were free cities, then Sardinian-administered; Monaco renounced them in 1861 (Menton page: 2 February 1861).

region.text: the fortress on the Rock of Monaco

ledger.note: 1297: Francesco Grimaldi seizes the Rock of Monaco under Genoese sovereignty. Monaco page: 'Monaco was first ruled by a member of the House of Grimaldi in 1297'; infobox 'House of Grimaldi, under the sovereignty of the Republic of Genoa: 8 January 1297'. The Rock had been refounded in 1215 as a Genoese colony.

region.text: the Rock of Monaco: 'Under Genoese control from 10 April 1301 to 12 September 1331'

ledger.note: April 1301: the Genoese evict Francesco Grimaldi and retake the Rock of Monaco. List of rulers of Monaco: François Grimaldi reigned from 8 January 1297 to 10 April 1301 and the Rock was 'Under Genoese control from 10 April 1301 to 12 September 1331'; Monaco page: 'Francesco was evicted a few years later by the Genoese forces'. The Grimaldi hold no other land in these years, so no shape is drawn for 1301-1330.

region.text: the Rock of Monaco: Charles I 'retook the Rock from the Genoese'

ledger.note: 12 September 1331: Charles I retakes the Rock of Monaco from the Genoese. List of rulers of Monaco: Charles I reigned from 12 September 1331 and 'retook the Rock from the Genoese'; Charles I page: 'Charles retook the Rock on 12 September 1331'.

region.text: the town of Menton: 'Acquired in 1346 by Charles Grimaldi, Lord of Monaco'

ledger.counterpart: Menton (previous holder not named by the page)
ledger.note: 1346: the Grimaldi acquire Menton. The Menton page gives the year and the buyer but not who held Menton before; the Monaco page speaks of annexing the towns 'between 1346 and 1355'. Charles I page (read 2026-10-25): 'In 1346 he acquired the Lordship of Menton'; it too names no previous holder, seller or price.

region.text: Roquebrune (Roccabruna): 'In 1355, Roccabruna fell under the control of the Grimaldi family of Monaco for five centuries'

ledger.counterpart: Roquebrune (previous holder not named by the page)
ledger.note: 1355: Roquebrune passes to the Grimaldi of Monaco. The Roquebrune page is silent on who held it before and on how the Grimaldi gained it. Charles I page (read 2026-10-25): 'in 1355, he conquered the Lordship of Roquebrune'; it names no previous holder.

region.text: the Rock of Monaco: 'Under Genoese control from 15 August 1357 to January 1395'; Menton and Roquebrune were 'retained' (List of rulers of Monaco)

ledger.note: 15 August 1357: Charles I dies and the Genoese take the Rock again; the Grimaldi keep Menton and Roquebrune. List of rulers of Monaco: Charles I reigned to 15 August 1357 and the Rock was 'Under Genoese control from 15 August 1357 to January 1395'; Rainier II 'Yielded Monaco to the besieging Genoese for 20,000 fl. but retained Menton and Roquebrune' (undated on the page, tied to this date by the reading that fits the table); Charles I page: the Rock 'was again conquered by the Genoese army'.

region.text: the Rock of Monaco: Louis, 'January 1395 - 19 December 1395' (List of rulers of Monaco)

ledger.note: January 1395: the Grimaldi hold the Rock again. List of rulers of Monaco: the Genoese control ran 'to January 1395' and Louis reigned from January 1395; the page gives no cause. The Monaco page's 'in the late 1300s Genoa lost Monaco after fighting the Crown of Aragon over Corsica' may describe this change.

region.text: the Rock of Monaco: 'Under Genoese control from 19 December 1395 to 11 May 1397' (List of rulers of Monaco)

ledger.note: 19 December 1395: the Genoese retake the Rock. List of rulers of Monaco: Louis's first reign ends 19 December 1395 and the Rock is 'Under Genoese control from 19 December 1395 to 11 May 1397'. Menton and Roquebrune are read as kept (Rainier II 'retained Menton and Roquebrune', undated).

region.text: the Rock of Monaco: Louis, '11 May 1397 - 5 November 1402' (List of rulers of Monaco)

ledger.note: 11 May 1397: the Grimaldi regain the Rock. List of rulers of Monaco: Louis reigned again from 11 May 1397, the Genoese control having ended on that date.

region.text: the Rock of Monaco: 'Under Genoese control from 5 November 1402 to 5 June 1419' (List of rulers of Monaco)

ledger.note: 5 November 1402: Louis's second reign ends and the Genoese hold the Rock again until 5 June 1419. Menton and Roquebrune are read as kept (Rainier II 'retained Menton and Roquebrune', undated).

region.text: the Rock of Monaco: Jean, Ambroise and Antoine 'bought back Monaco from Genoa' (List of rulers of Monaco)

ledger.note: 5 June 1419: the sons of Rainier II buy back Monaco and rule it jointly until 1427. List of rulers of Monaco: 'Sons of Rainier II, Jean, Ambroise and Antoine, bought back Monaco from Genoa'. Disagreement: the Monaco page says 'In 1419, the Grimaldi family purchased Monaco from the Crown of Aragon'; this ledger follows the list page, which names Genoa as the holder through 5 June 1419 (the Monaco page and History of Monaco do not date any Genoese control after the late 1300s, and History of Monaco never mentions Aragon in its medieval part).

region.text: Monaco: 'occupied by the Duchy of Milan under the governorship of Genoese Biagio Assereto from 3 October to November 1436' (List of rulers of Monaco)

ledger.note: 3 October 1436: troops of the Duchy of Milan under the Genoese governor Biagio Assereto occupy Monaco. List of rulers of Monaco: 'Monaco was occupied by the Duchy of Milan under the governorship of Genoese Biagio Assereto from 3 October to November 1436.' Monaco is the occupied party; the Grimaldi lordship continues.

region.text: Monaco: the Milanese occupation ended in November 1436 (List of rulers of Monaco)

ledger.note: November 1436: the Milanese occupation of Monaco ends; the page gives the month but no day.

1612: Honoré II begins to style himself Prince of Monaco. Monaco page: 'In 1612, Honoré II began to style himself "Prince" of Monaco.' The lordship becomes a principality in style; the territory is unchanged.

region.text: Monaco, Menton and Roquebrune: 'From 1793 to 1814 Monaco was taken over by France' as part of the département of Alpes-Maritimes

ledger.note: 1793: Revolutionary France takes Monaco, Menton and Roquebrune. History of Monaco: 'From 1793 to 1814 Monaco was taken over by France'; Monaco page: 'In 1793, Revolutionary forces captured Monaco'; Roquebrune page: 'In 1793, Roquebrune became French for the first time'. No page opened gives a month.

region.text: Monaco, Menton and Roquebrune restored to the Grimaldi: French control ran 'from 1793 to May 17, 1814'

ledger.note: May 1814: the Grimaldi return and the principality is restored after Napoleon's abdication. The Monaco page's infobox dates it 17 May 1814 'from the French Empire' and 17 June 1814 'from occupation of the Sixth Coalition'; the Menton page: 'In 1814, Menton was included in a reconstituted principality of Monaco'; Roquebrune 'was returned to Monaco in 1814'.

region.text: Menton and Roquebrune: 'In 1848, Menton, along with its neighbour Roquebrune, seceded from Monaco' (Menton page)

ledger.note: 1848: Menton and Roquebrune secede from Monaco and become free cities under the protection of the Savoy prince (Roquebrune page). They placed themselves under Sardinian protection 'two years later' (Menton page; History of Monaco says 1849). Neither page gives a month. Monaco keeps only its own 2 km2.

region.text: Menton and Roquebrune: Monaco 'renounced his rights in perpetuity on 2 February 1861'

ledger.note: 2 February 1861: the Prince of Monaco renounces Menton and Roquebrune to France for 4 million francs. Menton page: 'Napoleon III paid 4 million francs in compensation to the prince of Monaco, who renounced his rights in perpetuity on 2 February 1861'. The Monaco page's infobox dates the Franco-Monegasque Treaty 11 February 1861 and says it recognised Monaco's sovereignty; History of Monaco calls the land lost 'about 95% of its territory'. The towns were already French in fact after the plebiscite of 15-16 April 1860 (Menton page), so this event is the formal renunciation, not a new change of hands.

region.text: Monaco

ledger.note: 11 November 1942: the Italian Army occupies Monaco. History of Monaco: 'On 11 November 1942, the Italian Army invaded and occupied Monaco.' The Monaco page says only 'In 1943' and adds that Italy formed a fascist administration. Monaco is the occupied party; the state continues, neutral.

region.text: Monaco

ledger.note: September 1943: the Italian occupation gives way to a German one after Mussolini's fall. The page dates the German arrival, not the Italian withdrawal, so the end month is inferred from it.

region.text: Monaco

ledger.note: September 1943: the German Army occupies Monaco. History of Monaco: 'Soon after in September 1943, following Mussolini's fall in Italy, the German Army occupied Monaco'; the Monaco page: 'In September 1943, after Mussolini's fall from power, the German Wehrmacht occupied Italy and Monaco.'

region.text: Monaco

ledger.note: 3 September 1944: Allied forces liberate Monaco. History of Monaco: 'The country was liberated on 3 September 1944 by Allied forces.' In August 1944 the Germans had executed three Resistance leaders there.

wars.name: French Revolutionary Wars (capture of Monaco, 1793)

zones.text: Monaco, Menton and Roquebrune, annexed to the département of Alpes-Maritimes

wars.outcome: Revolutionary forces captured Monaco in 1793 and France held it, with Menton and Roquebrune, until the restoration of the Grimaldi in May 1814.
wars.note: The Monaco page says 'In 1793, Revolutionary forces captured Monaco and until 1814 it was occupied by the French' without naming the war or a battle; the war article was not opened (page budget), so the name is descriptive.

wars.name: Revolutions of 1848 (Menton and Roquebrune)

zones.text: Menton and Roquebrune, free cities from 1848, Sardinian-protected, voted to join France on 15-16 April 1860, renounced by Monaco on 2 February 1861

wars.outcome: Monaco lost Menton and Roquebrune, about 95% of its territory (History of Monaco), first to secession in 1848, then to France in 1860-1861 for 4 million francs.
wars.note: No fighting is recorded on the pages opened; Roquebrune page: after two years of independence the towns 'were administered by the House of Savoy for ten years'. Treaty of Turin of 24 March 1860 (Menton page) ceded the County of Nice to France.

wars.name: World War II
wars.outcome: Neutral Monaco was occupied by Italy on 11 November 1942 and by Germany in September 1943, and liberated by Allied forces on 3 September 1944.
wars.note: The Monaco page dates the Italian occupation 1943; History of Monaco gives 11 November 1942.

certainty.note: The Rock, Menton and Roquebrune are named towns; no page opened gives a boundary line. The Treaty of Péronne (1641) names the three places but draws no frontier. From 1301 to 1419 the Rock changed hands between Genoa and the Grimaldi eight times (four losses and four gains in the ledger); the dates are the list page's, the shapes are readings.

After the 1861 cession the principality is the small enclave of about 2 km2; the pages give no survey line, so 'sharp' rests on the treaty and the modern enclave. The Italian and German occupations (1942-1944) leave the frontier unchanged.

Re-read in the repair pass: 'Francesco was evicted a few years later by the Genoese forces'; 'in the late 1300s Genoa lost Monaco after fighting the Crown of Aragon over Corsica'; 'In 1419, the Grimaldi family purchased Monaco from the Crown of Aragon'.

sources.title: History of Monaco
sources.note: 1297, 1346, 1355, 1524 Spanish authority, 1641, 1793 to 17 May 1814, 1815-1817 Sardinian protectorate, 1848-1861, 'about 95% of its territory', and the World War II dates (11 November 1942, September 1943, 3 September 1944). Two fetches summarised the page differently; the dated sentences used here are the ones the fetches quoted. sources.title: Treaty of Péronne (1641)
sources.note: Signed 14 September 1641; France recognised the prince's sovereignty over Monaco, Menton and Roquebrune (Article 6), removed the Spanish garrison, French fiefs in compensation.

sources.title: Franco-Monegasque Treaty
sources.note: Thin: gives the year 1861 only, 4 million francs and 'recognised the sovereignty of Monaco'; no day, no signatories, no 1848. The Menton page was used for the 1861 date.

sources.title: Menton
sources.note: 1346 acquisition, 1814 restoration, 1848 secession, Sardinian protection two years later, Treaty of Turin 24 March 1860, plebiscite 15-16 April 1860, renunciation on 2 February 1861 for 4 million francs.

sources.title: Roquebrune-Cap-Martin
sources.note: 1355 Grimaldi control (seller not named), 1793 French, 1814 returned, 1848 free city, ten years of Savoy administration, cession to France in 1861.

sources.title: List of rulers of Monaco
sources.note: Repair pass for the review of eu-10-i: reign dates of every lord and prince and the Genoese spans (10 April 1301 to 12 September 1331, 15 August 1357 to January 1395, 19 December 1395 to 11 May 1397, 5 November 1402 to 5 June 1419), the Milan occupation of 1436. Read through WebFetch, whose summaries paraphrase the table; the quoted sentences are those the fetch returned verbatim and two separate fetches agreed on the dates.

sources.title: Charles I, Lord of Monaco
sources.note: Repair pass: 'Charles retook the Rock on 12 September 1331'; 'In 1346 he acquired the Lordship of Menton'; 'in 1355, he conquered the Lordship of Roquebrune'; died 15 August 1357 and the Rock 'was again conquered by the Genoese army'. Silent on the previous holders of Menton and Roquebrune, on Aragon and on any 20,000 florins.

notes:
Merged rows: Cliopatria has two rows for Wikidata Q235, 'Principality of Monaco' (1642-2024, 5 shapes) and 'Kingdom of Monaco' (1815-1939, 4 shapes). They are one state: Monaco was a principality throughout (every page opened calls it one; none calls it a kingdom) and the rows alternate without overlap (Principality 1642-1814, Kingdom 1815-1939, Principality 1945-2024) and carry the same polygons (164.4 km2, then 94.1 km2). One dossier under the earlier slug, both Names in cliopatria_names, all nine shapes reviewed. Nobody should write a separate kingdom-of-monaco dossier (the eu-20 briefs list it as owned); colours.json holds a colour for each slug and the kingdom's is unused.

Start: 1297, the Grimaldi seizure of the Rock (Monaco page infobox 8 January 1297), not Cliopatria's 1642. New keyframes cover the Rock 1297-1300 and 1331-1345, plus Menton 1346-1354, all three places 1355-1356, 1395, 1397-1401 and 1419-1641, and Menton and Roquebrune alone 1357-1394, 1396 and 1402-1418, when the Genoese held the Rock; nothing is drawn for 1301-1330 (see the next paragraph). If the project prefers sovereign statehood, the start would be 1641 (Treaty of Péronne, 14 September 1641) or 1633 (Spain's recognition of Honoré II, Monaco page); the ledger and keyframes from 1642 stand either way.

Cliopatria geometry: every Monaco polygon is wrong in size and the post-1848 ones are wrong in place. 164.4 km2 (1645-1847) for about 40 km2 of land; 94.1 km2 (1848-2024) and 47.0 km2 (1936-1939) for 2.084 km2, with a bbox of 7.15-7.23E that does not contain Monaco (7.41E, gazetteer) and France as the only modern country. I marked the post-1848 shapes wrong and gave the named country. The grid is about 253 km2 per cell, so a 2 km2 state is a single cell at best: {country: Monaco} resolves to one cell centred about 7.29E 43.85N, while the Cliopatria 1945 shape resolves to a different cell near 7.2E 43.71N, and radii under about 15 km around Monaco resolve to no cell. The rendering and gazetteer agents need a rule for sub-cell polities; a dossier cannot fix that.

Grimaldi rule interrupted 1301-1419 (repair pass after the review of eu-10-i): the List of rulers of Monaco gives the Genoese spans 'from 10 April 1301 to 12 September 1331', 'from 15 August 1357 to January 1395', 'from 19 December 1395 to 11 May 1397' and 'from 5 November 1402 to 5 June 1419', and the Monaco page says 'Francesco was evicted a few years later by the Genoese forces'. The ledger records four losses (1301-04, 1357-08, 1395-12, 1402-11) and four gains (1331-09, 1395-01, 1397-05, 1419-06) with republic-of-genoa as counterpart, and a one-month Milanese occupation (3 October to November 1436, duchy-of-milan). Nothing is drawn for 1301-1330 because the Grimaldi held no other land then; the state keeps its start year of 1297 and the map should show it as absent, not dissolved. If the project prefers an unbroken shape, the start could move to 1331 (the first year the Rock is held without a gap before Menton), but then the 1297 seizure would be lost. Keyframes start in the year of the event that creates them (1357, 1395 for the Rock regained in January, 1397, 1402, 1419); the months are in the ledger. The Rock-only reading of the 1357, 1395, 1402 losses rests on Rainier II's undated 'retained Menton and Roquebrune' (confidence 2). The seat of the Grimaldi while the Rock was Genoese is not given by any page opened, so identity.capitals leaves 1301-1330, 1357-1394, 1396 and 1402-1418 without a capital instead of inventing one. Page disagreement on the 1419 seller: the Monaco page says 'in the late 1300s Genoa lost Monaco after fighting the Crown of Aragon over Corsica' and 'In 1419, the Grimaldi family purchased Monaco from the Crown of Aragon', while the list page has Genoese control continuing through 5 June 1419 and the sons of Rainier II buying Monaco back 'from Genoa'; History of Monaco never mentions Aragon in its medieval section. The ledger follows the list page (dated per span, and it names Genoa as the seller); the Monaco page's Aragonese interlude is not drawn. On the same list page, Jean I 'gained sovereignty for Monaco' on 20 November 1441, which may mark the end of the Genoese sovereignty named in the 1297 infobox; no page opened says so. The list page also dates the French rule of 1793-1814 (the National Convention from 19 January 1793, annexation on 24 February 1793 as the fetch summarised it), which the ledger's 1793 loss does not yet carry as a month.

Gaps in Cliopatria that the dossier covers: 1297-1641 (new keyframes), 1794-1813 (right: France held Monaco; the ledger records the loss in 1793 and the gain in May 1814), 1940-1944 (new keyframe; the state continued, neutral, occupied from 11 November 1942).

Protectors and suzerains for the other dossiers (vassal_start/vassal_end belong to the suzerain, with 'principality-of-monaco' as counterpart): Genoese sovereignty from 1297 (Monaco page infobox); Spanish authority and garrison from 1524, 'an autonomous state for about a century' (History of Monaco; the page names the Treaty of Burgos and, inconsistently, the treaty of Tordesilla), Honoré II recognised by Spain in 1633 (Monaco page); French protection from the Treaty of Péronne, 14 September 1641 (500 French soldiers paid by the French crown under the prince's command, rent of 75,000 livres a year); Sardinian protectorate from the Congress of Vienna, 1815, confirmed by the Treaty of Stupinigi in 1817, ending in 1860 (Monaco page: 'Monaco remained in this position until 1860'); limited French protection from the July 1918 treaty, endorsed in 1919 (Monaco page); the 2002 treaty (Monaco independent if the dynasty ends). These are not in this ledger because the schema puts a vassal relation in the suzerain's ledger. The eu-13 (Sardinia, Genoa, Savoy) and France dossiers should carry them.

Disagreements between pages: (1) Sardinian protection of the free cities: History of Monaco says 1849, the Menton page 'two years later' than 1848 (1850), and Roquebrune says two years of independence then ten years of Savoy administration. (2) The formal 1861 act: Menton page 2 February 1861, Monaco infobox 11 February 1861 (Franco-Monegasque Treaty); both are February, the ledger uses month 2. (3) Roquebrune's 1861 'plebiscite' versus the Menton page's plebiscite of 15-16 April 1860 and payment in 1861. (4) Italian occupation: Monaco page 'In 1943', History of Monaco 11 November 1942; the ledger follows the dated sentence. (5) The Monaco page says the annexation of Menton and Roquebrune increased the territory 'by almost ten times', History of Monaco says the 1861 loss was 'about 95%' (a twentyfold ratio); the keyframe notes use 95%.

Seller of Menton (1346) and Roquebrune (1355): the Menton, Roquebrune, Monaco, History of Monaco and, in the repair pass, Charles I pages are silent ('In 1346 he acquired the Lordship of Menton'; 'in 1355, he conquered the Lordship of Roquebrune'), so the gain counterparts are plain strings, not slugs. 1645: no page explains Cliopatria's 141 to 164.4 km2 step; treated as a polygon artefact and corrected from the Treaty of Péronne, which names all three places in 1641.

Free cities of Menton and Roquebrune (1848-1860): a small entity with no Cliopatria row; the loss counterpart is its descriptive name. It may deserve a stub dossier (suggested slug free-cities-of-menton-and-roquebrune) or none; it was under Sardinian protection and administration, and France annexed it in 1860-1861.

Not collected: the 1911 constitution (5 January 1911, Monaco infobox) and the 1962 and 2002 acts, which move no border; Treaty of Burgos 1524 article; the French Revolutionary Wars article (the war name in wars[] is descriptive).

Pages: eight distinct pages opened in all (the original six plus List of rulers of Monaco and Charles I, Lord of Monaco in the repair pass, which also re-read Monaco and History of Monaco) against a budget of five; in the original run six opened against a budget of five (the merged Kingdom row adds four shapes and the extension to 1297 adds three keyframes; the Franco-Monegasque Treaty page proved a stub). Pages that failed: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Franco-Monegasque_Treaty_of_1861 and https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monaco_during_World_War_II (url_not_found).

Gazetteer names used that the gazetteer lacks: place Menton (France) and place Roquebrune-Cap-Martin (France). Radii of 4 km and 3 km are my reading, not a page's figure; at the grid's resolution they add little beyond the Monaco cell.
